q8.answer: The MERGE is guarded by updated_at: it updates only when stage.updated_at >= target.updated_at, and inserts when the order is new. Before that, step 6 dedupes the stage to the newest version per order_id. So an older or duplicate copy can never overwrite a newer one, and a re-run is a no-op for unchanged rows.

q9.answer: It is stored in etl.control, in the warehouse, in the single row pipeline='orders' (column high_water_mark). It is written inside the step 6 warehouse transaction, in the same commit as the MERGE and the run_log succeeded mark. The value is GREATEST(old HWM, max updated_at of the extracted rows), taken from the data and not the clock. If no rows came back it does not move.

q10.answer: The whole night's load (MERGE, HWM update, run_log mark) is one warehouse transaction in step 6. Dashboards read only committed analytics.orders, so they see the whole night or none of it. Staging happens in a separate table, etl.orders_stage, that dashboards never read.

q11.answer: A failed attempt is rolled back, so the target and HWM are unchanged, and its run_log row is marked failed. The next attempt empties etl.orders_stage at step 4, so no leftovers are seen. The retry reads the same unchanged HWM and extracts the same window, updated_at > HWM minus 2h, with no upper bound.

q12.answer: It re-extracts every row created on each mismatched day (by created_at, UTC) from the replica and loads them to stage. It applies them with the same updated_at-guarded MERGE, with all mismatched days in one transaction. It never touches the nightly high-water mark.
